lessonTitle: Interpreting Pathology Reports: Grade, Stage, Margins, Immunohistochemistry and Cervical Cytology

blocks.text: An oncologist opens a report that reads: invasive carcinoma, grade 2, pT1c pN0, margins clear by 4 mm, ER positive, HER2 negative. In one line it tells her what the tumour is, how aggressive it looks, how far it has spread, whether it was fully removed and which drug classes will work. This unit teaches you to read that sentence.

blocks.markdown: A histopathology report converts a glass slide into decisions. It has fixed sections: patient and clinical details, specimen type, macroscopic (gross) description, microscopic description and the final **diagnosis**, which should list tumour type, grade, stage, margin status and ancillary test results such as immunohistochemistry (IHC).

blocks.title: Grade, stage and margin
blocks.text: **Grade** describes how abnormal the tumour cells look (differentiation, proliferation) and predicts behaviour. **Stage** describes how far the tumour has spread, expressed by the TNM system: T is tumour size or local extent, N is regional lymph node involvement and M is distant metastasis; the prefix p means pathological (assessed on the resected specimen). **Margin status** records whether tumour reaches the cut surface; tumour at an inked margin is a positive margin (R1) and means residual disease may remain, whereas R0 means no tumour at the margin.

rows: Invasive carcinoma of no special type; squamous cell carcinoma
Clear by 4 mm; or tumour at inked margin (R1)
blocks.caption: The core elements of a cancer pathology report.

blocks.title: Extracting the key facts from a report
blocks.prompt: A report on a segmental colectomy states: adenocarcinoma, moderately differentiated; tumour invades through the muscularis propria into pericolic fat (pT3); 2 of 16 lymph nodes contain metastasis (pN1); lymphovascular invasion present; circumferential margin tumour-free at 3 mm. Summarise tumour type, grade, stage and margin status.

steps.text: Tumour type: adenocarcinoma (a gland-forming malignancy), the usual type in the colon.
Grade: moderately differentiated, which is intermediate (grade 2).
Stage: pT3 means invasion through the muscularis propria into pericolic tissue; pN1 means 1 to 3 regional nodes positive (2 of 16 here).
Margin: the circumferential margin is clear at 3 mm, so the resection is R0 on that margin; lymphovascular invasion is an adverse prognostic feature.

blocks.answer: Moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, pT3 pN1, margin clear (R0), with lymphovascular invasion.

blocks.markdown: **Histological grading in breast cancer** uses the Nottingham system. Three features are each scored 1 to 3: tubule (gland) formation, nuclear pleomorphism and mitotic count. The sum ranges from 3 to 9: scores 3 to 5 are grade 1, 6 to 7 are grade 2 and 8 to 9 are grade 3.

blocks.title: Nottingham grading
blocks.prompt: A tumour scores 3 for tubule formation, 3 for nuclear pleomorphism and 1 for mitotic count. Calculate the total score and assign a grade.

steps.text: Compare with the bands: 6 to 7 corresponds to grade 2.
Note that a high nuclear score is offset by a low mitotic count.

blocks.markdown: **Immunohistochemistry (IHC)** uses an antibody that binds a specific protein in tissue; a labelled enzyme reaction (commonly producing a brown chromogen, DAB) shows where the protein is. In diagnosis it identifies tissue of origin (for example cytokeratins for carcinoma, TTF-1 in many lung adenocarcinomas) and distinguishes look-alike tumours. In treatment selection it identifies targets: **oestrogen receptor (ER)** positivity predicts benefit from endocrine therapy, and **HER2** overexpression (3+) predicts benefit from HER2-directed therapy such as trastuzumab. **Ki-67** stains proliferating nuclei, and the Ki-67 index is the percentage of tumour nuclei that are positive.

blocks.latex: \text{Ki-67 index (\%)}=\frac{\text{positive tumour nuclei}}{\text{total tumour nuclei counted}}\times 100

blocks.markdown: **Cervical cytology screening.** Cervical cancer is caused by persistent infection with high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV), especially types 16 and 18. A brush samples exfoliated cells from the **transformation zone**, where columnar epithelium becomes squamous and where pre-malignancy begins. In liquid-based cytology the cells are examined for **dysplasia**: enlarged hyperchromatic nuclei, a high nuclear to cytoplasmic ratio and irregular chromatin. Results are graded as low-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (LSIL, corresponding to CIN 1) or high-grade (HSIL, CIN 2 to 3). Many programmes now test for high-risk HPV first and use cytology to triage positives.

rows: Mild change, often transient HPV effect
Follow-up or HPV testing per programme
blocks.caption: Cervical cytology results and actions (protocols vary by programme).

blocks.title: Screening detects pre-malignancy
blocks.text: Cytology is a screening test, not a diagnosis. An abnormal smear leads to colposcopy and biopsy, where histology confirms the grade of cervical intraepithelial neoplasia and treatment such as excision is planned.

points: A report states tumour type, grade, stage (pTNM), margin status and ancillary results; grade is cell abnormality, stage is spread.
Nottingham score is the sum of tubule, nuclear and mitotic scores, banded into grades 1 to 3.
IHC identifies origin and treatment targets such as ER and HER2; cervical cytology detects dysplasia in the transformation zone before cancer develops.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes grade from stage?

options.text: Grade describes how abnormal the cells look; stage describes the extent of spread
Grade describes the size of the specimen; stage describes the stain used
Grade describes the lymph node count only; stage describes the cell type
They are identical terms

questions.correctOptionText: Grade describes how abnormal the cells look; stage describes the extent of spread

distractorRationale.b: Specimen size and stains are not grade and stage.
distractorRationale.c: Nodes are part of stage, and cell type is tumour type.

questions.explanation: Grade reflects tumour cell differentiation and proliferation, whereas stage reflects anatomical extent through TNM. Both are prognostic but answer different questions.

questions.stem: A resection report for a rectal carcinoma states 'tumour present at the inked circumferential margin'. What is the implication?

options.text: The margin is positive (R1) and residual tumour is likely, so further treatment is considered
The specimen is unsuitable for diagnosis
The tumour is low grade
There is no lymph node involvement

questions.correctOptionText: The margin is positive (R1) and residual tumour is likely, so further treatment is considered

distractorRationale.a: Correct: tumour at the margin means incomplete excision.
distractorRationale.c: Margin status says nothing about grade.
distractorRationale.d: Margin status is separate from nodal status.

questions.explanation: Tumour at the inked margin means the surgeon cut through or at the tumour edge, so cells may remain in the patient. A positive margin guides re-excision, radiotherapy or other additional treatment.

questions.stem: How does immunohistochemistry show that a protein is present in tissue?

options.text: A specific antibody binds the protein and a labelled enzyme reaction produces visible colour
The tissue is dissolved and DNA sequenced
Red cells are counted in the section
The tissue is frozen and weighed

questions.correctOptionText: A specific antibody binds the protein and a labelled enzyme reaction produces visible colour

distractorRationale.c: Counting red cells is not IHC.

questions.explanation: IHC relies on antibody-antigen binding followed by an enzyme-linked colour reaction, which allows localisation of the protein within the tissue architecture.

questions.stem: A breast cancer shows strong, complete membrane staining (3+) for HER2 on IHC. Which treatment option does this result support?

options.text: HER2-directed therapy such as trastuzumab
Endocrine therapy as the only reason
Anti-VEGF therapy alone
No systemic treatment is relevant

distractorRationale.a: Correct: HER2 overexpression predicts benefit from anti-HER2 agents.
distractorRationale.b: ER status, not HER2, guides endocrine therapy.
distractorRationale.c: VEGF is unrelated to this IHC result.

questions.explanation: HER2 overexpression marks a tumour dependent on HER2 signalling, and antibody therapy targets this receptor. IHC therefore selects patients for a specific treatment.

questions.stem: Which cytological finding is characteristic of a high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion?

options.text: Cells with a high nuclear to cytoplasmic ratio and hyperchromatic irregular nuclei
Normal superficial squamous cells with small nuclei
Acute inflammatory cells only
Abundant mature glycogenated cytoplasm with tiny nuclei

questions.correctOptionText: Cells with a high nuclear to cytoplasmic ratio and hyperchromatic irregular nuclei
questions.explanation: Dysplastic cells have enlarged hyperchromatic nuclei relative to cytoplasm. The degree of nuclear to cytoplasmic disproportion increases from low-grade to high-grade lesions.

questions.stem: A cervical cytology result of HSIL is a diagnosis of invasive cancer and does not require colposcopy.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: HSIL indicates high-grade pre-malignant change, and it is followed by colposcopy and biopsy to confirm the lesion and plan treatment. Cytology is a screening test and cannot by itself diagnose invasion.

questions.stem: A pathologist counts 520 tumour nuclei and finds 156 stain positive for Ki-67. Calculate the Ki-67 index as a percentage.
questions.explanation: The index is 156 divided by 520, multiplied by 100, which is 30%. A higher index indicates more proliferating cells.

questions.stem: A breast carcinoma has tubule formation score 3, nuclear pleomorphism score 3 and mitotic count score 2 on the Nottingham system. What is the total score (dimensionless)? Scores 8 to 9 are grade 3.
questions.explanation: The total is 3 + 3 + 2, which is 8. A score of 8 falls in the 8 to 9 band, so the tumour is grade 3.

questions.stem: A 54-year-old woman has a wide local excision for breast cancer. The report states: invasive carcinoma of no special type, Nottingham grade 3, 24 mm, 1 of 4 sentinel nodes positive, margins 0.5 mm clear, ER negative, HER2 3+. Extract the key information and explain how the immunohistochemistry affects treatment.
markingGuide: Tumour type: invasive carcinoma of no special type
Grade 3, meaning poorly differentiated or high-grade
Stage details such as size 24 mm and 1 positive node (pN1)
Margin clear but close, with the distance reported
ER negative means endocrine therapy is not expected to be effective
HER2 3+ supports HER2-directed therapy such as trastuzumab
IHC determines treatment targets as well as diagnosis
questions.explanation: The report converts pathology into prognosis and treatment targets. Marking should reward correct separation of grade, stage and margin and a correct link of IHC to therapy.

questions.stem: Describe how cervical cytology screening detects pre-malignant change and what happens after an abnormal result.
markingGuide: High-risk HPV (16 and 18) persistence causes dysplasia
Brush sample from the transformation zone
Cells examined for increased nuclear to cytoplasmic ratio and nuclear abnormality
Classification into low-grade and high-grade lesions
Screening aims to find CIN before cancer develops
Abnormal result leads to colposcopy and biopsy for histological confirmation
Treatment such as excision of high-grade CIN
questions.explanation: The screening exploits the long pre-malignant phase of cervical neoplasia. Cytology identifies women who need biopsy, and histology gives the definitive diagnosis.
